[head=2][color=#e8b04b]Radio & Comms[/color][/head]
Your headset is your lifeline. In the Taypan hyperwar, the side that coordinates over the radio beats the side that does not. Each faction talks on its own encrypted channels, and you can only hear and speak on the channels your headset is keyed for.
[head=3][color=#e8b04b]Speaking on the radio[/color][/head]
- Prefix your message with a [color=#6ab7d6]semicolon (;)[/color] to talk on your default channel. - Prefix with a [color=#6ab7d6]colon (:)[/color] followed by a channel letter to speak on a specific channel. For example, [color=#6ab7d6]:i[/color] talks on the Imperial net. - [color=#6ab7d6]:h[/color] automatically uses your own faction or department channel, so you do not have to remember the letter.
[color=#8fc98a]Examine your headset[/color] at any time to see the exact channels and prefixes available to you, since these differ by faction and role.
[head=3][color=#e8b04b]Channel keys[/color][/head]
These are the prefixes for the main channels. You can only use the ones your headset is keyed for.
- [color=#684871]Imperial (DSM)[/color] command net uses [color=#6ab7d6]:i[/color], and the Imperial civilian net uses [color=#6ab7d6]:j[/color]. - [color=#bf4d00]NCWL[/color] uses [color=#6ab7d6]:o[/color]. - [color=#535961]Shinohara (SHI)[/color] uses [color=#6ab7d6]:w[/color]. - [color=#ff7f7f]Gorlex / Coalition (TFSC)[/color] uses [color=#6ab7d6]:p[/color]. Its member companies have their own nets, such as Cyberdawn on [color=#6ab7d6]:2[/color], Interdyne on [color=#6ab7d6]:3[/color], and SAW on [color=#6ab7d6]:x[/color]. - [bold]Command[/bold] channels are restricted to officers and leaders. The NCWL command net uses [color=#6ab7d6]:h[/color], and it is keyed only into command headsets.
[head=3][color=#e8b04b]Radio discipline[/color][/head]
- [color=#d9776c]The enemy cannot hear your faction net[/color], but a captured or looted enemy headset can. Watch what you say if your gear falls into enemy hands. - Keep the net clear during a fight. Short, clear callouts about positions, targets, and casualties save lives, while idle chatter gets people killed. - Report enemy movement, request support, and confirm orders. A quiet radio in a warzone usually means something has gone wrong.
